title: Search shows results for the previous keystroke
why: Typing 'tea' shows the right result for a split second, then the results for 'te' replace it. Whether it happens depends on network timing, so it's flaky by nature.
finding: Each keystroke sends its own /api/search request. The response for q=te arrived after the one for q=tea and overwrote it. The server returned 1 match for 'tea'; the list showed 4, including 'Write blog post'.
actual: The input shows 'tea' but the list shows '4 results' — the results for the earlier query 'te' (Plan team offsite, Update onboarding docs, Write blog post, Prepare investor update). The correct 'tea' result (1 task) is briefly shown and then replaced by the late-arriving 'te' response. 'Write blog post', which contains no 'tea', remains visible.
expected: After the input settles on 'tea', the list should show only the result(s) for 'tea'. The server returns exactly one task for /api/search?q=tea ('Plan team offsite'), so only that task should be displayed; non-matching tasks like 'Write blog post' should not appear.

reproduce.html: Open the app and click 'Search' in the sidebar.
In the 'Search tasks' input type a query whose intermediate prefixes match many tasks but whose final value matches few — e.g. type 'tea'.
Observe the results list after typing finishes.

rootCause.html: The Search view runs a useEffect keyed only on the query string that, for every change, issues GET /api/search?q=<query> and unconditionally writes the response into result state — useEffect(()=>{let t=e.trim();if(!t){r([]);return}a(!0),Or.search(t).then(e=>{r(e.results),a(!1)})},[e]), where search:e=>Dr(/search?q=${encodeURIComponent(e)}). The effect uses no AbortController and performs no check that the resolving response belongs to the current query, so the result state is set by whichever request resolves last rather than the most recent query. Because each keystroke starts its own request and the requests have varying durations, an earlier request can resolve after a later one and overwrite the correct results. For 'tea', /api/search?q=tea resolved at 31515ms but the earlier /api/search?q=te resolved later at 31712ms, so the stale 'te' results (4 tasks) replaced the correct 'tea' result (1 task) and remained on screen.

rootCauseSteps.html: Typing 'tea' fired three separate uncancelled requests: /api/search?q=t (start 30230ms), /api/search?q=te (start 30239ms, duration 1473ms, response-body at 31712ms) and /api/search?q=tea (start 30245ms, duration 1270ms, response-body at 31515ms). The requests therefore completed out of order: the later-issued 'tea' request finished ~197ms before the earlier-issued 'te' request.

title: Checkout charges the pre-discount total after a promo code
why: The button says Pay $117.00 and the order goes through. Only the amount charged is wrong, and only when the promo is applied after the checkout page has loaded.
finding: placeOrder is memoized with useCallback(…, [cart?.id]), so it kept the total from before the promo. POST /api/orders sent amount: 130 while the button read Pay $117.00, and order #10422 was charged $130.00.
actual: The POST /api/orders request body sends "amount":130 even though the pay button just read "Pay $117.00"; the server creates order #10422 with amount 130, and the order confirmation page displays "Total charged $130.00" with no discount amount shown — the applied WELCOME10 promo is silently dropped from the charged total.
expected: After applying WELCOME10 and seeing Total $117.00 / "Pay $117.00", placing the order should submit amount 117, and the order confirmation for Order #10422 should show the discounted total charged (e.g. $117.00 with the -$13.00 discount reflected), matching what the shopper agreed to pay at checkout.

why: React regenerates the tree on the client, so the page ends up looking right. The mismatch only exists between the server HTML and the first client render.
finding: Greeting.tsx creates new Date() in a useState initializer on both sides. The server rendered an afternoon hour and ‘Good afternoon’; the client rendered 8:55 PM and ‘Good evening’, so React threw #418.
actual: React error #418: Hydration failed. This error causes visual inconsistencies — the UI may not match what the server rendered Hydration failed. First occurrence: "Uncaught Error: Hydration failed because the server rendered text didn't match the client. As a result this tree will be regenerated on the client. This can happen if a SSR-ed Client Component used: -…". Suggested action: The server-rendered HTML doesn't match what the client renders. Common cause: using browser-only values (Date.now(), window.*) during SSR.
expected: The server-rendered HTML and the client's first (hydration) render should produce identical text — the hero <h1> should read the same greeting (e.g. "Good evening, Dana") during hydration, with no React error #418 and no regeneration of the server tree. chronology.html: Homepage first paint: the hero card shows "Good evening, Dana" with the local date/time "Monday, October 19 · 8:55:48 PM" below it. The server had rendered "Good afternoon" into the same <h1>, so React logged "Hydration failed because the server rendered text didn't match the client" (error #418) and regenerated the tree on the client — the visible text is the client's re-render, not the hydrated server HTML.

rootCause.html: components/Greeting.tsx initializes time-dependent state with a fresh Date on both server and client: line 12 const [now, setNow] = useState(() => new Date()), and the render at line 22 calls greetingFor(now.getHours()). The server rendered the page when now.getHours() fell in the 12–17 bucket, so greetingFor returned "Good afternoon"; the client's first render created a different Date (local time 8:55 PM, hour 20), so greetingFor returned "Good evening". The two text nodes for the same <h1> differ, hydration fails with React error #418, and React throws away the server tree and regenerates it on the client (onRecoverableError → recoverable hydration error).

title: Yjs provider sends 56 requests that can't succeed
why: The visible symptom is just 'Editor disconnected'. The retry storm behind it is invisible.
finding: The first PUT returned 530 'error code: 1016' at 107988ms. 37ms later the provider (Ry.ensureDocument) started re-POSTing awareness with no backoff: 56 times, all 530.
actual: The provider issues an unbounded series of POSTs to /api/yjs/docs/rooms/ws-apple-note-458f1c9f/v3/collaboration?awareness=default — 56 requests in this recording, starting 37ms after the initial PUT fails at 107988ms and continuing until the end of the session — and every single one returns HTTP 530 with body "error code: 1016". The editor status bar shows "Editor disconnected" and "Participants 0" throughout, and content typed by the user is never synced.
expected: The provider should treat the document-creation failure (HTTP 530, "error code: 1016") as terminal for the session after a bounded number of retries: stop re-POSTing to /v3/collaboration, surface a clear error to the user, and reuse a single pending request instead of re-issuing per sync/awareness update. The editor should show an explicit 'could not connect' error rather than silently hammering a dead origin.

chronology.html: The user has opened the app and created a new note; the app shows the editor screen. Immediately after, the Yjs provider attempts to create the collaboration document room for note ws-apple-note-458f1c9f via PUT /api/yjs/docs/rooms/ws-apple-note-458f1c9f/v3/collaboration.

Document creation fails: the PUT at 107988ms returns HTTP 530 ("error code: 1016"), and the provider immediately fires the first of the doomed POSTs to /api/yjs/docs/rooms/ws-apple-note-458f1c9f/v3/collaboration?awareness=default (108045ms and 108071ms, both 530). The editor status bar already shows "Editor disconnected" and "Participants 0". Two console errors record "Failed to create document: 530 error code: 1016". From here the POSTs repeat without pause — 56 in total, every one 530.

Over a minute later the provider is STILL re-POSTing to the same dead endpoint (POSTs continue at 122088ms, 127489ms, 132626ms, 141739ms…, all HTTP 530). The editor status bar still reads "Editor disconnected · Chat connecting · Participants 0"; the note is empty and the user's typing is never synced. The doomed request firehose runs for the rest of the recording with no backoff, no user-visible error, and no recovery.

rootCause.html: The Yjs provider class Ry in assets/main-BIfeKqPq.js has no failure handling for a dead sync origin: ensureDocument() throws ("Failed to create document: 530 error code: 1016", recorded in the console.error at [workspace-index] error / [yjs-provider] error), but the provider's update/awareness handlers keep calling the sync endpoint on every document update and awareness tick regardless. Because the connection never succeeds, the doc/awareness state never reaches "synced", so each local change and awareness ping re-queues another POST to the same /v3/collaboration URL — 56 identical POSTs, all answered HTTP 530 "error code: 1016", with no backoff, deduplication, or abort. The bug in the client is that failing sync is retried indefinitely instead of being detected, capped, and reported, so a dead origin turns into an endless firehose of doomed requests and an editor that never syncs.

title: Live sync re-downloads everything 258 times because the checkpoint never advances
why: Each request looks fine (200 OK). It's only wrong across the whole session.
finding: checkpoint=-1 on every round for about 160s: 258 back-to-back GETs to /pulls?live=1, about 631ms each, with only 2 clicks the whole time.
actual: The client sends checkpoint=-1 on every round for the whole session: 258 sequential GET requests to /api/repos/maple/reading-room/pulls (257 x HTTP 200, 1 no-response), each ~575–760ms, back-to-back with ~600–750ms between request starts, re-downloading/re-processing the same projection continuously while the user does nothing.
expected: A checkpoint-based live sync should send the most recently received checkpoint on each round so the server returns only new data since that checkpoint (or holds the request until there is new data). Once the projection is loaded, the client should reuse it and only fetch deltas, keeping network activity near zero while nothing changes.

chronology.html: The recording's network log shows a continuous sequential GET loop against /api/repos/maple/reading-room/pulls with checkpoint pinned at -1: requests at 15292ms, 15627ms, 16342ms, ... 175614ms — one starting as soon as the previous finishes, all 200, ~600–750ms cadence, while the user performs no interactions.

At the end of the recording (~175s), request #254 still carries the identical query checkpoint=-1, and 258 total requests to the endpoint have accumulated (257 x 200). The checkpoint cursor never advanced even once across the entire session, proving the loop re-fetches the full projection from the beginning every round.

rootCause.html: The live-sync client for the PR index never advances its checkpoint cursor: every long-poll round sends checkpoint=-1 (initial 'from the beginning' value) instead of the checkpoint returned by the previous response, so the server can never short-circuit an idle round with an empty delta and the client re-downloads and re-processes the full pulls projection ~every 600ms for the whole session (258 requests).

rootCause.html: In src/lib/dates.js, parseDateInput(value) returns new Date(value). For the date-only string '2026-10-20', new Date('2026-10-20') constructs a Date at UTC midnight (2026-10-20T00:00:00.000Z). Schedule.jsx line 77 (describe = (dateStr) => formatLongDate(parseDateInput(dateStr), language, timeZone)) then passes that instant to formatLongDate, which formats it with Intl.DateTimeFormat in the workspace timeZone 'America/New_York' (UTC-4 in October). At 2026-10-20T00:00:00Z it is 20:00 on 2026-10-19 in New York, so the preview renders 'lunes, 19 de octubre de 2026' — one day earlier than the selected date. The date-only input value must be parsed as a local (or UTC-timezone) date rather than left at UTC midnight when formatted in a non-UTC timezone.

rootCauseSteps.html: SearchSources 'parseDateInput' shows the function defined in src/lib/dates.js line 14 as return new Date(value) and that Schedule.jsx line 77 formats it via describe = (dateStr) => formatLongDate(parseDateInput(dateStr), language, timeZone), i.e. the preview's date goes through the UTC-midnight parse and the timezone-aware formatter.

Evaluating new Date('2026-10-20') in the workspace timezone proves the shift: the string parses to ISO 2026-10-20T00:00:00.000Z and Intl.DateTimeFormat with timeZone 'America/New_York' formats that instant as 'lunes, 19 de octubre de 2026'.

The visible state after the time selection confirms the defect: the date input holds '2026-10-20', the time select holds '09:30', and the rendered [data-testid=schedule-preview] element contains 'Reunión el lunes, 19 de octubre de 2026 a las 09:30' — the one-day-earlier date.

why: Undo looks like it worked: the button disables and the board re-renders. The snapshot it restored had already been changed by the edit it was meant to undo.
finding: SET_CHECK_ITEM sets item.done in place, and snapshot() only shallow-copies cards. A logpoint at boardReducer.js:55 returned sharedItemObject: true: the saved past state and the live board shared the same checklist item.

rootCause.html: The undo snapshot shares the very object that SET_CHECK_ITEM mutates. In http://localhost:3203/src/store/boardReducer.js the SET_CHECK_ITEM case (lines 48-56) finds the checklist item and writes item.done = action.done directly onto the existing item object, then records the pre-edit cards into state.past via record() -> history.js snapshot(). But snapshot() only shallow-copies each card ({ ...card }), so the recorded past snapshot shares the same checklist item objects as the live state. When the checkbox is toggled, the in-place mutation writes through to the snapshot that was just stored in state.past. The Logpoint at boardReducer.js:55 confirms this: the past snapshot's first checklist item is already done: true AND sharedItemObject: true (past snapshot item === current card item). When Undo then dispatches UNDO (boardReducer.js:86-91) it restores cards: state.past[state.past.length - 1] — which already contains done: true — so the badge stays "☑ 1/2" even though the past entry is consumed and the Undo button becomes disabled.

rootCauseSteps.html: Toggling the checklist checkbox dispatches SET_CHECK_ITEM, which in boardReducer.js mutates the existing checklist item in place (item.done = action.done, lines 48-56) and stores a snapshot of the cards into state.past; because history.js snapshot() shallow-copies cards ({ ...card }, lines 3-5), that stored snapshot shares the same (now-mutated) checklist item object — the Logpoint at boardReducer.js:55 returns pastDone [true, false] and sharedItemObject true for the "Customer interview synthesis" card.

Clicking Undo dispatches UNDO which restores cards from state.past[state.past.length-1] and slices the past entry; since the restored snapshot already contains done:true, the Review card badge stays "☑ 1/2" while the history entry is consumed — the Evaluate at the final frame returns undoDisabled:true and the badge text "☑ 1/2" still present.
